description: IA-58A Pucará displayed as A-581 (c/n 082, completed February 1983, retired April 1999) but a composite: fuselage of A-581 with wings from AX-06, gear doors from A-550 and rudder parts from A-559. Outdoors at the museum (pictorial January 2023).
aliases: Pucara; Pucará; c/n 082; AX-06; IA58; IA58A; AX06

description: A-4C Skyhawk C-302 (c/n 12631, ex BuNo 148438), delivered May 1976, retired 15 March 1999 and stored at Área Material Río Cuarto before transfer to Oliva; outdoors (pictorial January 2023).
Canberra B.62 B-102 (c/n 71233, ex-RAF WJ713), delivered November 1970, retired 1998 and sent to the museum; outdoors (pictorial January 2023).

IAI Dagger C-415 (c/n S-04), Malvinas veteran flown from San Julián and Río Grande in 1982, later modernised to Finger standard and retired December 2013; restored in 1982 markings with a plaque to 1st Lt Carlos Castillo. Described in 2023 as the most faithful Dagger restoration in Argentina (an earlier blog note claiming it is a disguised Mirage IIIEA is contradicted by the c/n).
Agusta A109A Hirundo AE-335 (c/n 7148), one of the Army A109s that went to the Malvinas in 1982; supplied by the Army in 2019 and photographed at Oliva April 2021.
Aérospatiale SA 330L Puma PA-13 (c/n 1598) of the Prefectura Naval Argentina, retired June 2011 and donated to the museum in 2022 (pictorial January 2023).

Fokker F28 Mk 3000C 0741/5-T-20 (c/n 11145, ex PH-EXV, later civil LV-RRA), which landed troops at Stanley on 2 April 1982 and flew 41 wartime links; moved by road from Ezeiza and presented at the museum on 2 April 2023.
